note: Curated metadata. Counts, duplicates and overlaps are computed by evaluation/build_manifest.py into evaluation/manifest.json. 'unknown' means unknown; nothing here has been independently verified.

role_definitions.unit_test_fixture: Data created only to exercise code paths in unit tests.
role_definitions.development_tuning: Data used (or documented as usable) while writing or tuning rules, the corpus or thresholds, or written by the same authors with knowledge of the detectors. Results on it are smoke tests.
role_definitions.historical_benchmark_result: Recorded outputs of earlier pipelines. Not input data; not evidence about the MVP.
role_definitions.held_out_evaluation: Data verified never to have been used for rule, corpus or threshold development. NO dataset currently qualifies.

datasets.title: Kavach-PB attack cases (Atomic Red Team + GTFOBins converted to tool calls)
datasets.label: attack
datasets.purpose: 519 malicious command-style tool calls used to measure VAULT/EXECUTOR hit rates during rule development.

provenance.documented_origin: 456 Atomic Red Team and 63 GTFOBins items converted into `tool:NAME args:{json}` strings by the project's own scripts (eval/naive_baseline/README.md on main; kavach_eval/reference_corpus_v0 on main). The conversion scripts have not been independently checked.
provenance.license: unknown (no licence recorded in the repository)

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: eval/agentharm_independent/README.md (main) states the VAULT/EXECUTOR rules were authored by mining detection misses on these corpora; the 519 call strings are identical to training_pairs_*_capped.jsonl (measured in docs/test-data-inventory.md).

datasets.label_semantics: Every row is malicious by construction (derived from attack-technique sources). Not human-verified. The file also holds `target_ministers` labels derived from the Kavach corpus and verdicts from the pre-MVP pipeline; both are ignored by the runner.
known_issues: Mapping of cases to ministers depends on the system under test.
Contains verdicts from an older pipeline; not MVP results.

context.notes: Bare tool calls. No user instruction, tool output or account email in the file.

datasets.title: BFCL general-purpose benign function calls
datasets.label: benign
datasets.purpose: 793 generic function-calling examples used as a zero-hard-block false-positive gate during development.

provenance.documented_origin: Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard items (`bfcl_simple_*`, `bfcl_live_simple` per kavach_eval/reference_corpus_v0 on main) rendered as tool calls by the project. No URL, version or licence recorded.
provenance.license: unknown (no licence recorded in the repository)

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: benchmarks/KAVACH_PB_VAULT_EXECUTOR_UPGRADE.md (main) uses it as the benign false-positive gate when evaluating rule layers; identical to training_pairs_bfcl_v0.jsonl negatives (measured).

datasets.label_semantics: All rows treated as benign. Generic function calls, not agent-security traffic.
known_issues: Not representative of the tool surfaces attacks target.

datasets.title: benign_v0: agent-shaped benign calls from one banking run
datasets.label: benign
datasets.purpose: 55 real tool calls (NotInject-style) from a qwen2.5:7b AgentDojo banking run, used to check false positives.

provenance.documented_origin: parliament/benign_test_set/README.md (main): calls copied verbatim from one live qwen2.5:7b run on AgentDojo's banking suite; 9 'clean' + 46 'goal_as_task' rows.
provenance.license: unknown (no licence recorded in the repository)

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: PROPOSED_vault_executor_expansion.py docstring (main): candidate rules were validated against 'benign_v0 55 + real_benign_trajectories + benign_probe 25' with zero tolerance.

datasets.label_semantics: Benign by construction (the user's own task requested the action). 'goal_as_task' rows reuse argument values that are malicious in AgentDojo's paired attack runs.
known_issues: Only 32 unique calls out of 55 rows.

context.notes: This checkpoint copy keeps only the call text. The same 55 cases WITH their user_task_text are registered as benign_v0_with_context.

datasets.title: benign_v0 rows with their user task text (same 55 cases as benign_v0_agent_shaped)
datasets.label: benign
datasets.purpose: The original benign_v0 file. Identical cases to benign_v0_agent_shaped (same order, same call text, checked), but carries user_task_text so CHANNEL can be given the user's instruction.

provenance.documented_origin: parliament/benign_test_set/README.md (main): built by build_v0.py from one live qwen2.5:7b AgentDojo banking run; 9 'clean' + 46 'goal_as_task' rows.
provenance.license: unknown (no licence recorded in the repository)

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: Same as benign_v0_agent_shaped: validation set for candidate VAULT/EXECUTOR rules.

datasets.label_semantics: Benign by construction. `goal_as_task` rows reuse argument values that are malicious in AgentDojo's paired attack runs; only the user task text distinguishes them.
known_issues: Duplicates benign_v0_agent_shaped on purpose: the pair lets you see the effect of supplying user_instruction. Do not add the two together.

present_but_not_mapped: why_legitimate (author annotations about the label; deliberately not sent)
context.notes: No tool outputs or account_email in the file.

datasets.title: 22 real benign banking sessions (same run as benign_v0)
datasets.label: benign
datasets.purpose: Session-level benign sequences for checking CHANNEL does not taint or block ordinary banking tasks.

provenance.documented_origin: parliament/benign_test_set/README.md (main): raw extraction of every qwen2.5:7b tool call from one live AgentDojo banking run.
provenance.license: unknown (no licence recorded in the repository)

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: Same calls as benign_v0 (32 unique calls across 64); used to validate CHANNEL provenance and VAULT/EXECUTOR candidate rules.

datasets.label_semantics: Benign sessions. Kept in tests/data (already part of the MVP unit tests); not duplicated.
known_issues: Single suite (banking). Zero benign coverage elsewhere (VALIDATION_PROTOCOL.md on main).
No tool outputs or user instruction are supplied to CHANNEL by the runner.

context.notes: 2 of 64 calls have a null tool_output and are sent without one. No account_email exists in this banking data.

datasets.title: AtriumOS author-written generalization audit
datasets.purpose: 36 paired scenarios (18 attack / 18 benign) with invented tool vocabulary, meant to test generalization beyond known rule keywords.

provenance.documented_origin: Generated by benchmarks/data/build_atriumos_scenarios.py (main), written by the project team; labels assigned from first principles by the author.

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: The builder's docstring says labels were assigned after reading prefilters.py, channel_taint.py and the NAVIGATOR corpus, so the author knew the mechanisms; the CHANNEL generalization fix was later verified against this set (injecagent_full_1054_rerun README, main).

datasets.label_semantics: ground_truth ATTACK -> attack, BENIGN -> benign (author-assigned). CHANNEL scenarios are two-call sessions.

context.notes: Calls only; CHANNEL scenarios are two-call sessions with no outputs or instruction.

datasets.title: OpenClaw-native hand-written scenarios
datasets.purpose: 30 cases (20 expected BLOCK, 10 expected ALLOW) in the exact `tool:exec args:{...}` format the corpus was designed for.

provenance.documented_origin: Hand-written by the project team (benchmarks/openclaw_native/run_native_benchmark.py docstring on main); two cases cite CVE-2026-25253.

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: The runner's docstring says the cases are 'written in the exact format the corpus was designed for'; overlap with specific rules is not measured.

datasets.label_semantics: expected BLOCK -> attack, expected ALLOW -> benign. Note the file's own ALLOW expectation: its original runner accepted ESCALATE on benign; this harness reports ESCALATE separately.

datasets.title: 50 hand-written benign developer sessions
datasets.label: benign
datasets.purpose: 93 benign actions (editing, testing, git, package management) used as a false-positive gate for corpus aggressiveness.

provenance.documented_origin: Hand-written in benchmarks/benign_traces.py (main): 'written by hand here (not generated from any model output)'. The copy is renamed .py.txt so it cannot be imported; content is byte-identical.

overlap_with_rule_development.evidence: The file states it is the FPR gate that runs before any InjecAgent run and that FPR > 5% means the corpus is too aggressive.

present_but_not_mapped: session.intent (author-written description of the session's purpose; not shown to be the instruction a user gave an agent, so it is NOT treated as user_instruction)
context.notes: Hand-written actions with no tool outputs.
